title: Bridget Marquardt Says the Playboy Mansion Was Haunted as She Talks Passion for Ghost Hunting (Exclusive)
excerpt: The former star of ‘The Girls Next Door’ shares why the paranormal feels normal to her as she stars in the horror comedy ‘Don’t F--- with Ghosts!’
content:
Gillian Telling

Tue, October 20, 2026 at 8:15 PM UTC

NEED TO KNOW

  • Bridget Marquardt, the Playboy personality, now hosts Ghost Magnet and appears in the comedy horror film Don’t F--- with Ghosts! and the series The Great American Ghost Hunt

  • Her fascination with the paranormal began at age 12 after using an Ouija board

  • Marquardt also claims she has seen a ghost at the Playboy Mansion

Bridget Marquardt, the former Playboy personality who starred in the series The Girls Next Door, is leaning into her surprising new passion project: ghost hunting.

“We call it paranormal because we don’t understand it, but it’s very normal,” Marquardt says of chasing spirits in her spare time and hosting the paranormal podcast Ghost Magnet with Bridget Marquardt. (She also hosts the Girls Next Level podcast with Holly Madison, her former costar on The Girls Next Door.)

Asked if she thought Playboy mansion, her onetime home, was haunted, she says yes. “I had one of my best paranormal experiences there,” Marquardt, 53, tells PEOPLE.

She remembers being with her sister and a friend named Stacy after returning from a trip to North Carolina, where she’d picked up a new puppy. “We’re all sitting on the bed talking,” she recalls. “And out of the corner of our eye, in the doorway to the bathroom, there is a woman standing there.”

The three women gasped — but when Marquardt turned to look directly at the mysterious visitor, she says, nobody was there. Her sister began crying, while her friend was too frightened to look again. What made the experience even stranger, Marquardt says, was that she recognized the woman.

“I recognized her as somebody who had been there before I even was living at the mansion,” she says. Marquardt says she’d met the woman during an earlier visit to the mansion in 1998 and had spent hours chatting with her. When she returned in 2001, she learned that the woman, who had worked as one of the mansion’s social secretaries, had died of cancer. “I think she just sort of came to see the new puppy in the house,” she says.

As for whether ex Hugh Hefner has ever visited her, she says sometimes. “I don’t try to summon him, but sometimes he appears in certain things,” she says, noting that it once happened when she was with Madison. “She was like, ‘No I don’t want to talk to him!’ so we just sort of sent the spirit away.” (Hefner died in 2017 at age 91.)

Marquardt says she’s been fascinated with ghosts ever since she was 12 and got her first Ouija board. Not long after, she began seeing her great grandfather all over the house.

“Half my family thought I needed to see a psychiatrist, and the other half thought I needed to see the pastor at our church,” she says. “Instead of scaring me away from the paranormal, it made me want to have another experience and prove to people that this isn’t weird.”

Which is why she was the perfect person to team up with filmmakers Stu Stone and Adam Rodness on their comedy horror Don’t F--- with Ghosts, in which two skeptics visit supposedly haunted locations in Canada.

Stone says he knew he had to have his old friend Marquardt involved somehow. “Bridget is the real deal,” he says of her ghost-hunting career.

“She’s got the equipment, she’s got the gear. And she take a different approach where she’s so friendly and inviting to the spirits,” he continues.

“Now we’ve shot a spinoff series called The Great American Ghost Hunt, where Bridget takes myself and Adam and celebrities on their first ghost hunts,” Stone adds.

After the film, he says he’s now “a believer.”

“I’ve seen stuff,” he says. “I’ve experienced stuff that I never thought I would. I’m definitely a believer.”

Don’t F--- with Ghosts is now streaming on Prime Video. The Great American Ghost Hunt streams on YouTube’s Potluck Originals on Wednesday, Oct. 21.
